BURHAN:v1p253#2/r12.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p253#2/r12.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p253#2/r12.claim: The source notes two verses beginning يا أيها الإنسان, one asking what deceived the person about the generous Lord and one saying the person labors toward the Lord.
BURHAN:v1p253#2/r12.anchor: وفيه ﴿ يا أيها الإنسان ما غرك بربك الكريم ﴾ ﴿ يا أيها الإنسان إنك كادح ﴾

QUSHAYRI:v3p405/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p405/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p405/r3.claim: Every accountable person labors toward God and will meet the recompense: good for good and evil for evil.
QUSHAYRI:v3p405/r3.anchor: إنك ساع بما لك سعيا ستلقى جزاءه ؛ بالخير خيرا وبالشر شرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p433/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p433/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p433/r1.claim: Kadhḥ is exertion that marks the self, from the verb for scratching skin; Ibn Muqbil and another poet illustrate the usage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p433/r1.anchor: الكدح: جهد النفس في العمل حتى يؤثر فيها، من كدح جلده إذا خدشه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p436/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p436/r7.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p436/r7.claim: Muqatil says “the human” is al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Asad, who argued with his brother Abu Salama about resurrection; the generic wording still includes everyone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p436/r7.anchor: وقال مقاتل: المراد به الأسود بن عبد الأسد بن هلال المخزومي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p436/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p436/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p436/r8.claim: Another identification is Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who labored for worldly gain, harmed the Messenger, and persisted in disbelief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p436/r8.anchor: وقيل: المراد أبي بن خلف، كان يكدح في طلب الدنيا وإيذاء الرسول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p436/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p436/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p436/r9.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects the remote view that the address singles out the Prophet's toil in conveying revelation and enduring harm, rewarded at his meeting with God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p436/r9.anchor: وأبعد من ذهب إلى أنه الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم، والمعنى: إنك تكدح

BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.claim: Al-Inshiqāq continues the close of al-Muṭaffifīn: allies enjoy reward and enemies receive punishment because they denied resurrection and judgment before their Creator-King.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.anchor: مقصودها الدلالة على آخر المطففين من أن الأولياء ينعمون والأعداء يعذبون ، لأنهم كانوا لا يقرون بالبعث ولا بالعرض على الملك الذي أوجدهم ورباهم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#2#s084/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#2#s084/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#2#s084/r5.claim: The two conditional openings have an obvious omitted answer: every person will be judged for all their striving, with disbelievers repaid and Muslims rewarded.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#2#s084/r5.anchor: والجواب محذوف _ لأنه في غاية الانكشاف بما دل عليه المقام مع ما تقدم من المطففين وما قبلها من السور

BIQAI-FULL:v8p368#s084/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p368#s084/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p368#s084/r3.claim: The singular address treats humanity as a kind before turning to every individual; receiving one’s record in the right hand marks acceptance as a believer and obedient servant.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p368#s084/r3.anchor: فمن كان مقبولا أعطي كتاب حسناته بيمينه لأنه كان في الدنيا من أهل اليمين أي الدين المرضي

NAHHAS:v5p185/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p185/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p185/r5.claim: The phrase is an adjective to ayy; al-Akhfash instead calls it a necessary connective.
NAHHAS:v5p185/r5.anchor: نعت لأي والأخفش يقول صلة لأنه لا بد منه

NAHHAS:v5p185/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p185/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p185/r6.claim: Kadhan is a verbal noun carrying emphatic force.

NAHHAS:v5p185/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p185/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p185/r7.claim: Famulāqīhi is nominative; its original ḍamma was omitted either for heaviness or because yā resembles an unvowelled alif.
NAHHAS:v5p185/r7.anchor: في موضع رفع والأصل ضم الياء فحذفت الضمة لثقلها

NAHHAS:v5p185/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p185/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p185/r8.claim: Some Arabs omit even fatḥa from yā, treating it like alif and leaving it unvowelled.
NAHHAS:v5p185/r8.anchor: ومن العرب من يحذف منها الفتحة فيجريها مجرى الألف فلا يحركها بحال

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r24.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r24.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r24.claim: Al-Inshiqāq begins with human toil and successive ordeals, whereas al-Tīn begins by honoring humanity; its fa therefore suits the emphasis on continuing, unclouded reward.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r24.anchor: في حين بدأ في سورة الين بتكريم الإنسان فقال: {لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الإنسان في أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ} فناسب ذلك تأكيد استمرار أجره وعدم تنغيصه

TABRISI:84:1-25/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:1-25/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:84:1-25/r12.claim: Kadh means strenuous striving and persistent work; a bull's hide marks are called kaduḥ from intense effort, with Ibn Muqbil as evidence.
TABRISI:84:1-25/r12.anchor: والكدح السعي الشديد في الأمر والدأب في العمل

TABRISI:84:1-25/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:1-25/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:84:1-25/r13.claim: Hawr is return or reversal, as in returning from increase to deficiency and in the expression about returning after being wound up.
TABRISI:84:1-25/r13.anchor: والحور الرجوع حار يحور إذا رجع

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:84:6-16/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:84:6-16/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:84:6-16/r1.claim: People labor for their Lord and ultimately meet their deeds at Resurrection.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:84:6-16/r1.anchor: { يا أيها الإنسان إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا } عامل لربك عملا { فملاقيه } فملاق عملك

ELMALILI:84:1-21#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:84:1-21#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:84:1-21#2/r11.claim: Commentators differ on the idha clauses: they may be adverbial without an answer, answer an implied question about recompense, omit an answer for awe, mean everyone learns their deeds, or contain their answer in the obedience verbs.
ELMALILI:84:1-21#2/r11.anchor: Bazıları bu اِذَا’ların şart mânasından mücerred zarfiyye olup cevâba muhtaç olmadığını söylemişlerdir

ELMALILI:84:1-21#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:84:1-21#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:84:1-21#2/r12.claim: The best answer to the clauses is found in one of the following two verses.
ELMALILI:84:1-21#2/r12.anchor: Fakat en doğrusu cevap şu iki âyetten birinin mazmûnundadır

ELMALILI:84:1-21#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:84:1-21#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:84:1-21#2/r13.claim: Kedh means scratching or exerting serious effort in good or evil; throughout life and after death people strive toward an outcome from their Lord, painful or pleasant.
ELMALILI:84:1-21#2/r13.anchor: tırmalamak ve kendisine tesir edecek vechile

ELMALILI:84:1-21#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:84:1-21#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:84:1-21#2/r14.claim: Some take famulaqihi as the answer to the idha clauses, while others make verse 6 itself the answer; the author prefers treating verse 6 as parenthetical and verse 7 as the answer.
ELMALILI:84:1-21#2/r14.anchor: Fakat en doğrusu cevap şu iki âyetten birinin mazmûnundadır

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p241/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p241/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p241/r4.claim: Though humanity is addressed generally, the warning particularly targets conceited people absorbed in worldly life, who are inevitably being drawn to meet their Lord.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p241/r4.anchor: Although the address of this sūrah is general

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p242/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p242/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p242/r1.claim: Kadh means to strive with great labor; human life is an unbroken journey from birth through changing stages and conditions to death, regardless of status.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p242/r1.anchor: to make an effort in something with great labour.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p242/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p242/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p242/r2.claim: Meeting the Lord is the purpose of life's journey: people must be held accountable, the objective for which this world was created.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p242/r2.anchor: The purpose of this meeting is obviously to hold them accountable for their deeds

STUDYQURAN:84:6/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:84:6/r1.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās
STUDYQURAN:84:6/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says every deed, good or bad, will be met with God.
STUDYQURAN:84:6/r1.anchor: According to Ibn ʿAbbās, this verse means, “Whatever deed you do, you will meet God with it, whether it is good or bad”

STUDYQURAN:84:6/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:84:6/r2.speaker: Maybudī
STUDYQURAN:84:6/r2.claim: Maybudī understands the verse as urging mindfulness because every moment brings one closer to God.
STUDYQURAN:84:6/r2.anchor: Maybudī understands it as an injunction to be mindful, since every moment is a step closer to God

TAB-FULL:v24p235/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p235/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p235/r1.claim: He links the preceding account of the sky splitting to the human seeing the good or evil he sent ahead, explaining that meaning through this verse and those that follow.
TAB-FULL:v24p235/r1.anchor: ومعنى الكلام: إذا السماء انشقت رأى الإنسان ما قدم من خير أو شر، وقد بين ذلك قوله

TABATABAI:84:1-6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:84:1-6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:84:1-6/r1.claim: The Meccan surah describes the Hour and humanity's journey to its Lord for an account based on the record, with warning predominating over glad tidings.
TABATABAI:84:1-6/r1.anchor: بيان تشير السورة إلى قيام الساعة، وتذكر أن للإنسان سيرا إلى ربه

TABATABAI:84:1-6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:84:1-6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:84:1-6/r2.claim: The conditional in verse 1 has an omitted result, supplied by verse 6: humanity meets its Lord, who reckons and recompenses it for its deeds.
TABATABAI:84:1-6/r2.anchor: والتقدير لاقى الإنسان ربه فحاسبه وجازاه على ما عمل

TABATABAI:84:1-6/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:84:1-6/r10.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:84:1-6/r10.claim: Al-Raghib defines kadh as striving and exertion.

TABATABAI:84:1-6/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:84:1-6/r11.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:84:1-6/r11.claim: Another definition is exerting the self in work until the work leaves an effect on it; the preposition ila gives the expression a sense of journey.
TABATABAI:84:1-6/r11.anchor: ففي الكدح معنى السير على أي حال

TABATABAI:84:1-6/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:84:1-6/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:84:1-6/r12.claim: The servant, as owned and governed by God, journeys toward his Lord; he should will and do only what his Lord commands and is accountable for his choices and acts.
TABATABAI:84:1-6/r12.anchor: فإن العبد لا يملك لنفسه إرادة ولا عملا فعليه أن يريد ولا يعمل إلا ما أراده ربه ومولاه وأمره به فهو مسؤول عن إرادته وعمله

TABATABAI:84:1-6/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:84:1-6/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:84:1-6/r13.claim: The verse argues for resurrection: lordship entails servitude, servitude entails responsibility, responsibility requires return and accounting, and accounting entails recompense.
TABATABAI:84:1-6/r13.anchor: يتضمن حجة على المعاد لما عرفت أن الربوبية لا تتم إلا مع عبودية ولا تتم العبودية إلا مع مسؤولية ولا تتم مسؤولية إلا برجوع وحساب

TABATABAI:84:1-6/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:84:1-6/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:84:1-6/r14.claim: Meeting God means reaching a state where only His judgment rules and nothing can screen the human from his Lord.
TABATABAI:84:1-6/r14.anchor: المراد بملاقاته انتهاؤه إلى حيث لا حكم إلا حكمه من غير أن يحجبه عن ربه حاجب

TABATABAI:84:1-6/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:84:1-6/r15.speaker: author
TABATABAI:84:1-6/r15.claim: The addressee is humanity as a whole, since God's lordship applies universally to every human.
TABATABAI:84:1-6/r15.anchor: المخاطب في الآية هو الإنسان بما أنه إنسان فالمراد به الجنس وذلك أن الربوبية عامة لكل إنسان

TABRISI:84:6/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:6/r6.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:84:6/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the response to إذا is indicated by فملاقيه; the pronoun can refer to the Lord or to a person’s labor and deed.
TABRISI:84:6/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج: جواب إذا يدل عليه قوله

TABRISI:84:6/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:6/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:84:6/r7.claim: An alternative grammatical view takes إلى as meaning لام.
TABRISI:84:6/r7.anchor: قيل: إن هنا إلى بمعنى اللام

TABRISI:84:6/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:6/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:84:6/r8.claim: The author prefers construing إلى according to the phrase’s meaning: the person is striving toward God.
TABRISI:84:6/r8.anchor: والوجه الصحيح فيه أن يكون محمولا على المعنى

TABRISI:84:6/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:6/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:84:6/r9.claim: Another possible construction attaches إلى to an omitted phrase: a person labors for himself and arrives at his Lord.
TABRISI:84:6/r9.anchor: على أنه يحتمل أن يكون إلى متعلقة بمحذوف ويكون التقدير أنك كادح لنفسك

TABRISI:84:6/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:6/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:84:6/r10.claim: The construction is compared with تبتل إليه, understood as turning from creation back to God or desiring Him.
TABRISI:84:6/r10.anchor: يكون على معنى تبتل من الخلق راجعا إلى الله تعالى أو راغبا إليه

TABRISI:84:6#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:6#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:84:6#2/r4.claim: The address is to every accountable descendant of Adam: each person labors through hardship in deeds and carries that work to God.
TABRISI:84:6#2/r4.anchor: خطاب لجميع المكلفين من ولد آدم يقول الله لهم سبحانه ولكل واحد منهم يا أيها الإنسان

TABRISI:84:6-8/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:6-8/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:84:6-8/r1.claim: Meeting the recompense is described as meeting the deed itself, magnifying its importance.
TABRISI:84:6-8/r1.anchor: أي ملاق جزاءه جعل لقاء جزاء العمل لقاء له تفخيما لشأنه

TABRISI:84:6-8/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:6-8/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:84:6-8/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes the pronoun to mean meeting the Lord and coming under His judgment, since He alone judges.
TABRISI:84:6-8/r2.anchor: وقيل: معناه ملاق ربك أي صائر إلى حكمه حيث لا حكم إلا حكمه

BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r3.claim: The address applies to every accountable person—believer, unbeliever, or sinner—individually, more emphatically than an undifferentiated plural address.
BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r3.anchor: جنس الإنسان الشامل للمؤمن والكافر والعاصي فالخطاب عام لكل مكلف على سبيل البدل

BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r4.claim: Kadhḥ is strenuous effort that affects the self; the related words denote hardship, toil, and severe striving, from the image of scratching the skin.
BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r4.anchor: الكدح جهد النفس في العمل والكد فيه بحيث يؤثر فيها والجهد بالفتح

BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r5.claim: Every person labors with difficulty toward meeting the Lord, meaning the time of meeting at death and the subsequent states represented as meeting.
BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r5.anchor: والمعنى إنك جاهد ومجد أي ساع باجتهاد ومشقة إلى لقاء ربك أي إلى وقت لقائه

BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r6.claim: When asked how to labor after the pens had dried and destinies been decreed, the Prophet said to act, for each person is made easy for what he was created to do.
BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r6.anchor: فقال اعملوا فكل ميسر لما خلق له

BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r7.claim: The person will inevitably meet the reward of his good or evil work, with no evasion or escape; worldly effort is in reality a path to its afterlife recompense.
BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r7.anchor: فملاق له أي لجزاء عملك من خير وشر عقيب ذلك لا محالة

BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r8.claim: One should undertake worldly actions that save one in the hereafter and avoid those that bring ruin, shame, and disgrace.
BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r8.anchor: فعليك أن تباشر في الدنيا بما ينجيك في العقبى واحذر عما يهلكك فيها

BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r9.claim: A hadith says the remorseful await mercy, the self-admiring await condemnation, and every worker will advance to what he sent ahead.
BURSEVI:v10p291#2/r9.anchor: وفي الحديث النادم ينتظرالرحمة والمعجب ينتظر المقت وكل عامل سيقدم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats the answer to إذا and the following events as effectively omitted because their sense is familiar throughout the Qurʾān; the human's encounter with reward or punishment supplies the meaning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r2.anchor: قال الفراء: وجواب {إذا السماء انشقت} وما بعده كالمتروك؛ لأن المعنى معروف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the answer to إذا is indicated by فملاقيه: on the Day of Resurrection, the person meets his deed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r3.anchor: ونحو هذا قال الزجاج: وجواب {إذا} يدل عليه قوله عز وجل: {فملاقيه}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r4.claim: In Arabic, kadhḥ is striving and persistent work in worldly and afterlife affairs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r4.anchor: معنى الكدح في اللغة: السعي والدؤوب في العمل في باب الدنيا والآخرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r5.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r5.claim: Al-Layth defines kadhḥ as a person's work, whether good or evil.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r5.anchor: وقال الليث: الكدح عمل الإنسان من الخير والشر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r6.claim: Abū ʿUbayda glosses “he strives for his livelihood” as exerting oneself and cites Ibn Muqbil's use of أكدح for laboring in pursuit of a living.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r6.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: فلان يكدح في عيشه (¬6) أي يجهد، وأنشد (¬7) لابن مقبل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r7.speaker: الكلبي والضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r7.claim: Al-Kalbī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say the person is doing work for his Lord.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r7.anchor: قال الكلبي (¬10)، # (والضحاك) (1) (2): إنك عامل لربك عملا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r8.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r8.claim: Muqātil says the person is journeying toward his Lord through his deeds.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p355#2/r8.anchor: وقال مقاتل: ساع بعملك إلى ربك سعيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p357/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p357/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p357/r1.claim: Abū Isḥāq takes the object of “meeting” to be the Lord.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p357/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p357/r2.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p357/r2.claim: An alternative explanation takes the object to be the person's deed.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p357/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p357/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p357/r3.claim: Al-Wāḥidī concludes that the intended meeting is the reward for one's deed.

QASHANI:84:1-6/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:84:1-6/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:84:1-6/r3.claim: The human being strives toward the Lord through death, moving swiftly with each breath, or by exerting effort in good or evil deeds.
QASHANI:84:1-6/r3.anchor: ساع مجتهد في الذهاب إليه بالموت

QASHANI:84:1-6/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:84:1-6/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:84:1-6/r4.claim: The pronoun in “meeting him” can refer either to the Lord or to the exertion, whose harmful consequence the person meets.
QASHANI:84:1-6/r4.anchor: { فملاقيه } ضررة، والضمير إما للرب وإما للكدح

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:84:6/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:84:6/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:84:6/r1.claim: Human life consists entirely of efforts, though their aims and nature differ, and all efforts end with God; no one remains forever, and God alone will call people to account.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:84:6/r1.anchor: İnsan bilmelidir ki dünya hayatı bütünüyle –mahiyetleri ve amaçları farklı da olsa– türlü çabalardan ibarettir; çabaların sonu da Allah’a varır

TUSTARI:84:6/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:84:6/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:84:6/r1.claim: A person strives toward the Lord through deeds and encounters Him in connection with that striving.
TUSTARI:84:6/r1.anchor: أي ساع بعملك إلى ربك سعيا

TUSTARI:84:6/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:84:6/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:84:6/r2.claim: Examine whether one's striving suits the Garden and nearness to God, or the Fire and distance from Him.
TUSTARI:84:6/r2.anchor: فانظر في سعيك يصلح للجنة ولقربه أم للنار وبعده

TUSTARI:84:6/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:84:6/r3.speaker: كهمس
TUSTARI:84:6/r3.claim: Kamhas said he wept for forty years after taking a piece from a neighbor's wall for his guest to wash his hand, after buying the guest grilled fish for one daniq.
TUSTARI:84:6/r3.anchor: وقد قال عمارة ابن زادان: قال لي كهمس: يا أبا سلمة أذنبت ذنبا فأنا أبكي عليه منذ أربعين سنة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r9.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r9.claim: The human laboring toward his Lord in al-Inshiqāq is identified as al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Asad.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r9.anchor: والثاني عشر : الأسود بن عبد الأسد

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p521#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p521#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p521#3/r1.claim: Kādiḥ means one who works hard and exerts himself in earning a living.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p521#3/r1.anchor: {إنك كادح} أي عامل ناصب في معيشتك؛ {إلى} لقاء {ربك}

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p521#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p521#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p521#3/r2.claim: He reads “to your Lord” as “to meet your Lord.”
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p521#3/r2.anchor: {إنك كادح} أي عامل ناصب في معيشتك؛ {إلى} لقاء {ربك}

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p70/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p70/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p70/r5.claim: The address is generic, as in O human, striving toward your Lord; God formed and proportioned people in whatever forms He chose, in beauty, ugliness, whiteness, blackness, dark complexion, or redness.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p70/r5.anchor: كما يقول القائل: يا أيها الرجل، وكلكم ذلك الرجل

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p167/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p167/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p167/r7.claim: A singular form may address a collective; the author cites 'O human' and 'you are striving' alongside the statement about harm touching a person.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p167/r7.anchor: وحد وهو يريد الجمع، كما قال: يا أيها الإنسان ما غرك بربك الكريم (6)

SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari defines كدح as exerting oneself in work until the effort leaves an effect, like scratching the skin; كادح means striving toward meeting the Lord, namely death.
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " جهد النفس [في العمل] والكد فيه، حتى يؤثر فيها

SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r2.speaker: ابن مقبل
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r2.claim: Ibn Muqbil's line uses أكدح for striving to live, illustrating the word's sense of exertion.
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r2.anchor: وقال ابن مقبل: 4524 وما الدهر إلا تارتان فمنهما أموت وأخرى أبتغي العيش أكدح

SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r3.claim: A second poet's line likewise uses أكدح for laboring through life.
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r3.anchor: وقال آخر: 4525 ومضت بشاشة كل عيش صالح وبقيت أكدح للحياة وأنصب

SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r4.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r4.claim: Al-Raghib says كدح can be used with the sense of كدم, biting with the teeth.
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r4.anchor: وقال الراغب: " وقد يستعمل الكدح استعمال الكدم بالأسنان

SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r5.speaker: الخليل
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r5.claim: Al-Khalil distinguishes the terms by saying كدح is less than كدم.

SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r6.claim: فملاقيه may coordinate with كادح, with an evident causal relation.
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r6.anchor: يجوز أن يكون عطفا على كادح. والتسبيب فيه ظاهر

SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r7.claim: Alternatively, it is the predicate of an omitted subject: فأنت ملاقيه.
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون خبر مبتدأ مضمر، أي: فأنت ملاقيه

SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r8.claim: The phrase may also be a response to a conditional, as discussed earlier.
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r8.anchor: وقد تقدم أنه يجوز أن يكون جوابا للشرط

SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r9.claim: Ibn Atiyya takes ف as coordinating a new clause with the previous sentence and reconstructs فأنت ملاقيه, with the pronoun returning to your effort.
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " فالفاء على هذا عاطفة جملة الكلام على التي قبلها. والتقدير: فأنت ملاقيه " يعني بقوله: " على هذا " ، أي: على عود الضمير على كدحك

SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r10.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r10.claim: The Shaykh says Ibn Atiyya's clause coordination is not necessary; the phrase can coordinate individual elements.
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r10.anchor: قال الشيخ: " ولا يتعين ما قاله، بل يجوز أن يكون من عطف المفردات "

SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r11.claim: The pronoun in ملاقيه may refer to the Lord or to the effort, in which case it means meeting the recompense for the effort.
SAMIN-DURR:84:6/r11.anchor: والضمير: إما للرب، وإما للكدح، أي: ملاق جزاء كدحك

ZAJJAJ:v5p303/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p303/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p303/r2.claim: The answer to idhā is indicated by famulāqīhi: when Resurrection comes, a person meets his deed.
ZAJJAJ:v5p303/r2.anchor: المعنى إذا كان يوم القيامة لقي الإنسان عمله

ZAJJAJ:v5p303/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p303/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p303/r8.claim: Tafsīr explains the phrase as doing work for one's Lord and meeting that work.
ZAJJAJ:v5p303/r8.anchor: جاء في التفسير إنك عامل لربك عملا فملاقيه

ZAJJAJ:v5p303/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p303/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p303/r9.claim: Another tafsīr explanation is striving toward one's Lord and meeting Him.
ZAJJAJ:v5p303/r9.anchor: وجاء أيضا: ساع إلى ربك سعيا فملاقيه

ZAJJAJ:v5p303/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p303/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p303/r10.claim: In Arabic, kadhḥ is exertion and persistent effort in work, whether worldly or otherworldly.

ZAJJAJ:v5p303/r11.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p303/r11.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p303/r11.claim: Tamīm ibn Muqbil's phrase akdaḥ illustrates striving and toil in seeking a livelihood.
ZAJJAJ:v5p303/r11.anchor: قال تميم بن مقبل: وما الدهر إلا تارتان فمنهما. . . أموت وأخرى أبتغي العيش أكدح

ZAJJAJ:v5p303/r12.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p303/r12.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p303/r12.claim: Another reported explanation takes the object of “meeting” to be one's work.

ASAD-NOTES:84:1#n4/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:84:1#n4/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:84:1#n4/r1.claim: Asad says earthly life is painful toil for everyone, whether consciously recognized or not, because sorrow, pain, drudgery, and worry outweigh rare happiness; this toil leads to meeting God at resurrection.
ASAD-NOTES:84:1#n4/r1.anchor: sorrow, pain, drudgery and worry by far outweigh the rare moments of true happiness and satisfaction

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p237/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p237/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p237/r1.claim: Islahi links al-Inshiqāq with al-Muṭaffifīn: both warn deniers of recompense and describe two final groups, with right-hand recipients succeeding and left-hand recipients disgraced.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p237/r1.anchor: the rejecters of reward and punishment are warned in the previous sūrah

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p237/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p237/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p237/r2.claim: Both sūrahs address affluent people who deny judgment or expect worldly honor in the afterlife; innate awareness of justice and the world's purpose require a final separation, dooming those who ignore it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p237/r2.anchor: Both sūrahs address the affluent and wealthy sections of the society

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p237/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p237/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p237/r3.claim: The preceding sūrah reasons from human nature, whereas al-Inshiqāq reasons from signs in the physical world.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p237/r3.anchor: The basis of reasoning in the previous sūrah is human nature

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p237/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p237/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p237/r5.claim: Man is rebuked for being inexorably drawn toward meeting his Lord and fate; those given their accounts in their right hands will have an easy, happy reckoning.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p237/r5.anchor: Man is rebuked that he is being relentlessly pulled to encounter His Lord

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p371#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p371#2/r8.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p371#2/r8.claim: Another view makes verse 84:6 the apodosis: when the sky splits, each striver meets what he has done.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p371#2/r8.anchor: وقيل جوابه: "يا أيها الإنسان إنك كادح"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p374/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p374/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p374/r1.claim: Kadḥ is a person's striving and effort in good or evil until it leaves an effect on him; the human is striving toward his Lord through his deeds.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p374/r1.anchor: أي ساع إليه في عملك، والكدح: عمل الإنسان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p374/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p374/r2.speaker: قتادة والكلبي والضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p374/r2.claim: Qatāda, al-Kalbī, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk explain it as doing deeds for one's Lord.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p374/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة والكلبي والضحاك: عامل لربك عملا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p374/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p374/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p374/r3.claim: Everyone meets the recompense of their deeds, whether good or evil.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p374/r3.anchor: أي ملاقي جزاء عملك خيرا كان أو شرا

BAYDAWI-FULL:84:6-12/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:6-12/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:6-12/r1.claim: One parsing makes the person meet his own effort; toil is strenuous work that leaves a mark, from the verb meaning to scratch.
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:6-12/r1.anchor: وتقديره لاقى الإنسان كدحه أي جهدا يؤثر فيه من كدحه إذا خدشه

BAYDAWI-FULL:84:6-12/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:6-12/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:6-12/r2.claim: Alternatively, the person meets God, while the statement that he toils toward his Lord is parenthetical; his toil is pursuit of the meeting with his recompense.
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:6-12/r2.anchor: والكدح إليه السعي إلى لقاء جزائه

DURR-FULL:v8p455/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p455/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p455/r6.claim: Qatada interprets striving toward God as working deeds for Him.
DURR-FULL:v8p455/r6.anchor: وفي قوله: {يا أيها الإنسان إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا} قال: عامل له عملا

DURR-FULL:v8p455/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p455/r7.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p455/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak likewise says a person works deeds toward his Lord.
DURR-FULL:v8p455/r7.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة عن الضحاك {يا أيها الإنسان إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا} قال: عامل إلى ربك عملا

DURR-FULL:v8p455/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p455/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p455/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says the person works and then meets his work.
DURR-FULL:v8p455/r8.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن ابن عباس في قوله: {إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا} قال: عامل عملا {فملاقيه} قال: ملاق عملك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p218/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p218/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p218/r1.claim: Because idhā attaches to part of the sentence and contains a conditional sense, “O human, you are striving” is treated as its answer; the conditional and answer each govern the other in different respects.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p218/r1.anchor: ولكن لما تعلق { إذا } بجزء من جملة { إنك كادح } وكانت { إذا } ظرفا متضمنا معنى الشرط صار : يا أيها الإنسان إنك كادح جوابا لشرط { إذا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p218/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p218/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p218/r2.claim: Idhā refers to future time, while its clause uses a past verb to mark the condition’s occurrence as certain, since idhā itself signals decisiveness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p218/r2.anchor: و { إذا } ظرف للزمان المستقبل ، والفعل الذي في الجملة المضافة إليه { إذا } مؤول بالمستقبل وصيغ بالمضي للتنبيه على تحقق وقوعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p220/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p220/r5.speaker: المبرد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p220/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad treats the address through “you will meet Him” as the answer to idhā, with the final clause as the main point and the striving clause as an insertion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p220/r5.anchor: وجملة : { يا أيها الإنسان إنك كادح } إلى آخره جواب { إذا } باعتبار ما فرع عليه من قوله : { فملاقيه } ونسب هذا إلى المبرد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p220/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p220/r6.speaker: المبرد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p220/r6.claim: On al-Mubarrad’s parse, when the sky splits and the earth is spread, the human meets his Lord after striving toward Him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p220/r6.anchor: فالمعنى : إذا السماء انشقت وإذا الأرض مدت لاقيت ربك أيها الإنسان بعد كدحك لملاقاته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p220/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p220/r7.speaker: المبرد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p220/r7.claim: Al-Mubarrad also allows the answer to be omitted and inferred from “you will meet Him”: the implied answer is “you will meet.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p220/r7.anchor: دل عليه قوله : { فملاقيه } والتقدير : إذا السماء انشقت إلى آخره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r1.claim: The primary purpose is to warn polytheists because they denied resurrection; for believers the address is a reminder and glad tidings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r1.anchor: والمقصود الأول من هذا وعيد المشركين لأنهم الذين كذبوا بالبعث . فالخطاب بالنسبة إليهم زيادة للإنذار ، وهو بالنسبة إلى المؤمنين تذكير وتبشير .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r2.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r2.claim: One reported view identifies the addressed person as al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Asad; Ibn ʿĀshūr notes variant spellings in biographical and exegetical works.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r2.anchor: فقيل : هو الأسود بن عبد الأسد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r3.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r3.claim: Another reported identification is Ubayy ibn Khalaf.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r4.claim: Either named individual may have occasioned the revelation, or one may have been intended from the outset.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r4.anchor: وقد يكون أحدهما سبب النزول أو هو ملحوظ ابتداء .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r5.claim: The root k-d-ḥ has several possible senses, and Ibn ʿĀshūr says its exact original meaning cannot be determined confidently.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r5.anchor: والكدح : يطلق على معان كثيرة لا نتحقق أيها الحقيقة ، وقد أهمل هذه المادة في ( الأساس )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r6.speaker: الراغب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r6.claim: Al-Rāghib’s apparent definition is exhausting oneself through work and toil.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r6.anchor: وظاهر كلام الراغب أن حقيقته : إتعاب النفس في العمل والكد .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r7.claim: The preposition ilā suggests an action that ends at meeting God; kadiḥ may be understood as “striving,” making the phrase a predicate of inna.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r7.anchor: وتعليق مجروره في هذه الآية بحرف ( إلى ) تؤذن بأن المراد به عمل ينتهي إلى لقاء الله ، فيجوز أن يضمن { كادح } معنى ساع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r8.claim: On the “striving” sense, daily work reaches toward tomorrow until life ends in death, which returns the person to God; thus striving ends in meeting Him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r8.anchor: وذلك يتقضى به زمن العمر الذي هو أجل حياة كل إنسان ويعقبه الموت الذي هو رجوع نفس الإنسان إلى محض تصرف الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r9.claim: Alternatively, kadiḥ may mean “walking”; then the phrase with ilā is an adverbial adjunct rather than a predicate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن يضمن { كادح } معنى ماش فيكون المجرور ظرفا لغوا .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r10.claim: Kadhan is an accusative cognate object emphasizing kadiḥ, construed with the sense “striving toward God”; the striving is unavoidable.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r10.anchor: و { كدحا } منصوب على المفعولية المطلقة لتأكيد { كادح } المضمن معنى ساع إلى ربك ، أي ساع إليه لا محالة ولا مفر .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r11.claim: The object pronoun in “meeting Him” refers to the Lord; no one escapes meeting God, hence the emphatic inna.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r11.anchor: وضمير النصب في ( ملاقيه ) عائد إلى الرب ، أي فملاق ربك ، أي لا مفر لك من لقاء الله ولذلك أكد الخبر بإن .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p456#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p456#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p456#2/r15.claim: The address is to humanity as a whole.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p456#2/r15.anchor: وقوله تعالى: يا أيها الإنسان مخاطبة للجنس،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p456#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p456#2/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p456#2/r16.claim: A kādiḥ works intensely, quickly, and with effort.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r1.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r1.claim: The Prophet says a person who asks despite having enough comes on Judgment Day with facial scratches or kduh marks.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r1.anchor: ومنه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من سأل وله ما يغنيه حاءت مسألته خدوشا أو كدوحا في وجهه يوم القيامة»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r2.speaker: الشاعر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r2.claim: A poem calls humans deluded and says they labor through life in a low state.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r3.claim: People labor in good or evil but inevitably travel to God; life flies by, so the verse warns them to act righteously.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r3.anchor: والمعنى أنك عامل خيرا أو شرا وأنت لا محالة في ذلك سائر إلى ربك،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r4.speaker: طلحة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r4.claim: Talha assimilates the kāf of كادح into the following min.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r4.anchor: وقرأ طلحة: بإدغام كاف كادح ومن هذه اللفظة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r5.claim: Qatada says whoever can make his labor obedience to God should do so.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة: من استطاع أن يكون كدحه في طاعة الله فليفعل،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r6.claim: The person meets his punishment or reward.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r6.anchor: وقوله تعالى: فملاقيه معناه: فملاقي عذابه أو تنعيمه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r8.speaker: آخرون منهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r8.claim: Other grammarians make فملاقيه the عامل; some experts posit an implicit verb.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r8.anchor: وقال آخرون منهم: العامل فملاقيه، وقال بعض حذاقهم: العامل فعل مضمر،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r9.speaker: كثير من النحاة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r9.claim: Many grammarians say the answer to إذا is omitted because the listener knows it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r9.anchor: فقال كثير من النحاة: هو محذوف لعلم السامع به،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r10.speaker: أبو العباس المبرد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r10.claim: Al-Mubarrad and al-Akhfash take the answer as يا أيها الإنسان إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا فملاقيه.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r10.anchor: وقال أبو العباس المبرد والأخفش: هو في قوله: يا أيها الإنسان إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا فملاقيه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r11.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r11.claim: Another analysis estimates an initial فاء before يا أيها الإنسان, with the answer in that implied particle.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r11.anchor: وقيل التقدير فيا أيها الإنسان، وجواب إذا في الفاء المقدرة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r13.speaker: جمهور المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r13.claim: Most exegetes say the pronoun refers to the Lord, linking meeting Him to laboring.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r13.anchor: فقال جمهور المتأولين هو عائد على الرب،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r14.speaker: بعض الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r14.claim: Some say it refers to labor itself: one meets it, meaning its reward, good or bad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p457/r14.anchor: وقال بعض الناس: هو عائد على الكدح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p356/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p356/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p356/r2.claim: People strive and work on the way to their Lord, then meet what they did, whether good or evil.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p356/r2.anchor: أي: ساع إلى ربك سعيا، وعامل عملا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p356/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p356/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p356/r3.claim: Jābir reports a saying attributed to Gabriel to Muḥammad: live as you wish because you will die, love as you wish because you will part, and act as you wish because you will meet your deeds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p356/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "قال جبريل: يا محمد، عش ما شئت فإنك ميت، وأحبب ما شئت فإنك مفارقه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p356/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p356/r4.speaker: بعض الناس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p356/r4.claim: Some take the pronoun to refer to the Lord, so the person meets his Lord and is recompensed for his striving; Ibn Kathir says this and the meeting of one’s deeds are compatible.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p356/r4.anchor: ومن الناس من يعيد الضمير على قوله: {ربك} أي: فملاق (4) ربك، ومعناه: فيجازيك بعملك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p356/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p356/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p356/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says a person does work with which he will meet God, whether it is good or evil.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p356/r5.anchor: قال العوفي، عن ابن عباس: {يا أيها الإنسان إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا} يقول: تعمل عملا تلقى الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p356/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p356/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p356/r6.claim: Qatada says human striving is weak and urges whoever can to make that striving obedience to God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p356/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: {يا أيها الإنسان إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا} إن كدحك-يا ابن آدم-لضعيف، فمن استطاع

JISHUMI:v10p7338/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7338/r1.speaker: المبرد
JISHUMI:v10p7338/r1.claim: Al-Mubarrad proposes fronting and delay, construing ‘when the sky splits’ after the clause about a person striving toward and meeting his Lord.
JISHUMI:v10p7338/r1.anchor: وقال المبرد: فيه تقديم وتأخير تقديره: يا أيها الإنسان، إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا فملاقيه إذا السماء انشقت.

JISHUMI:v10p7338/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7338/r4.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v10p7338/r4.claim: One occasion-of-revelation report says ‘O human’ was revealed concerning al-Ḥarith ibn ʿAmr al-Qurashi.
JISHUMI:v10p7338/r4.anchor: قيل: نزل قوله: (ياأيها الإنسان) في الحارث بن عمرو القرشي.

JISHUMI:v10p7338/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7338/r5.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v10p7338/r5.claim: Another view says the address applies generally.

JISHUMI:v10p7341/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7341/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7341/r4.claim: Every person striving in life will meet the recompense for his deeds.
JISHUMI:v10p7341/r4.anchor: ومنها: أن كل ساع يلقى جزاء عمله.

MUQATIL:84:6-8/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:84:6-8/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:84:6-8/r1.claim: The human being addressed is al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Asad; striving to his Lord means exerting himself toward Him and meeting Him with his deeds.
MUQATIL:84:6-8/r1.anchor: يعني بالإنسان الأسود بن عبد الأسد { إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا } إنك ساع إلى ربك سعيا

MUQATIL:84:6-8/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:84:6-8/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:84:6-8/r4.claim: At the Resurrection, creatures surge among one another for 300 years; then the Lord sits on the Throne to judge, with the angels arrayed in ranks, and they see Paradise and Hell.
MUQATIL:84:6-8/r4.anchor: فإنهم يموج بعضهم في بعض، مقدار ثلاث مائة سنة، حتى إذا استوى الرب جل وعز على كرسيه ليحاسب خلقه

QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r1.claim: Al-insan means humankind generally, addressed as “son of Adam.”
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { يأيها الإنسان إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا } المراد بالإنسان الجنس أي يابن آدم

QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r2.speaker: سعيد عن قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r2.claim: Sa'id reports Qatada's exhortation: son of Adam, your striving is weak; if able, make it striving in obedience to God, with no power except by God.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r2.anchor: وكذا روى سعيد عن قتادة: ياابن آدم، إن كدحك لضعيف، فمن استطاع أن يكون كدحه في طاعة الله فليفعل

QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r3.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r3.claim: Muqatil identifies the human as al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Asad.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r3.anchor: وقيل: هو معين قال مقاتل: يعني الأسود بن عبد الأسد

QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r4.claim: Another identification is Ubayy ibn Khalaf; another takes the address as all unbelievers, addressed as “O unbeliever.”
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r4.anchor: ويقال: يعني أبي بن خلف. ويقال: يعني جميع الكفار أيها الكافر إنك كادح

QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r5.claim: In Arabic, kadh means work and earning.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r5.anchor: والكدح في كلام العرب: العمل والكسب قال ابن مقبل

QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r6.speaker: ابن مقبل
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r6.claim: Ibn Muqbil's line uses akdahu for striving to earn a living through life's turns.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r6.anchor: قال ابن مقبل: وما الدهر إلا تارتان فمنهما أموت وأخرى أبتغي العيش أكدح

QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r7.claim: A second poetic citation likewise uses akdahu to mean working and striving for life.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r7.anchor: قال آخر: ومضت بشاشة كل عيش صالح وبقيت أكدح للحياة وأنصب أي أعمل

QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r8.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak reports Ibn Abbas's gloss: you are inevitably returning to your Lord, and kadh means return.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r8.anchor: روى الضحاك عن ابن عباس: «إنك كادح» أي راجع «إلى ربك كدحا» أي رجوعا لا محالة

QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r9.speaker: القتبي
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r9.claim: Al-Qutbi says the person works and labors in his livelihood until meeting his Lord, and meets Him bearing his deeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r9.anchor: القتبي «إنك كادح» أي عامل ناصب في معيشتك إلى لقاء ربك. والملاقاة بمعنى اللقاء أي تلقى ربك بعملك

QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r10.claim: Another explanation is that the person meets his record of deeds, since the work is over; the following verse's book-taking supports this.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:6-9/r10.anchor: وقيل أي تلاقي كتاب عملك لأن العمل قد انقضى ولهذا قال: « فأما من أوتي كتابه بيمينه»
